title: Persepolis
description:
Persepolis - 2001

Photographed just outside the ruins of Persepolis in southern Iran, this image contrasts thousands of years of history with a modern car park behind the camera. While the ruins have been captured countless times, this perspective is unique. Shot entirely on film with no digital manipulation, the effect comes purely from exposure, depth of field, and film speed. Particularly striking as a Giclée Hahnemühle German Etching print, its velvety surface holds the ink and light beautifully.


• Media:

	Original Art:	• 35 mm Transparency

title: Salvador
description:
Dali - 2002

Three artists impressed me most as a young boy: Dalí, Picasso, and Gaudí. This is the Dali portrait, with a matching one of Picasso.

It took me years to find a way to pay tribute visually. It finally came together after 30 years, in 2002. As for Gaudí, I still haven’t found the right approach, and I’m not sure I ever will.

title: Pablo
description:
Picasso - 2002

Three artists impressed me most as a young boy: Dalí, Picasso, and Gaudí. This is the Picasso portrait, with a matching one of Dalí.

It took me years to find a way to pay tribute visually. It finally came together after 30 years, in 2002. As for Gaudí, I still haven’t found the right approach, and I’m not sure I ever will.

title: You
description:
You - 2003

This represents how I imagine life: intersecting dimensions, each its own universe. Their overlap is the life of the individual, the life form standing before it. In that moment, all dimensions are active, creating a one-time connection between image and viewer.
